env.name: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE
env.notes: node-gyp ships gyp/pylib and CPython writes __pycache__/*.pyc beside any module it imports. The jail refuses correctly and the build succeeds either way, because bytecode is a pure cache — but the refused writes were counted as side effects and made nine native packages (keccak, lz4, ssh2, ...) demand write.userHome, the second-widest grant, when bytecode was the ENTIRE delta between arms. Setting this stops the write happening at all, which is the general fix; the harness previously filtered .pyc after the fact, which is the same fix re-derived per tool.

env.name: npm_config_logs_max
env.notes: npm writes a timestamped debug log to $HOME/.npm/_logs on failure, and nothing about it belongs to the package being measured. MEASURED in the top-100 sweep: '.npm/_logs' derived as a writePaths entry for FOUR unrelated packages, which would ship four per-package grants for a diagnostic byproduct of the installer. The same directory already caused one wrong diagnosis: its timestamped FILENAME varied between control runs and read as nondeterminism, which is what motivated the double-control union. Setting logs-max to 0 stops npm creating the file at all — the same shape as PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE above, and preferred over a harness filter for the same reason: it fixes the cause once for every tool rather than hiding the effect per tool. VERIFIED: a failing install writes 1 log file by default and 0 with this set.

env.name: npm_config_update_notifier
env.notes: npm stamps $HOME/.npm/_update-notifier-last-checked when it checks for a newer npm. It is npm's own housekeeping and has nothing to do with the package under test, but a lifecycle script that shells out to npm causes it, and the write then has to be BOUGHT with a grant. MEASURED: it is one of only two paths unrs-resolver was denied — the other being the native binary it legitimately writes into a dependency's store entry — so the package's grant was partly paying for npm's update check. Third entry of the same shape as the two above: stop the write at its cause rather than filtering the effect per package. VERIFIED: the file is created by default and absent with this set.
